boundedResearchDiscipline.note: No unresolved requirement bundle required more than four genuinely-evaluated candidates before an adequate source was accepted or an alternative bundle was tried. Several access failures (blocked/paywalled/unreadable candidates, listed below) were encountered and abandoned honestly rather than substituted with a search-summary or snippet as evidence.

accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.workaround: Abandoned; electrical quantity-symbol conventions were instead evidenced from electronics-tutorials.ws (AUTHORITATIVE_TECHNICAL_REFERENCE) and the EOLSS encyclopedia chapter (AUTHORITATIVE_TECHNICAL_REFERENCE), both genuinely retrieved and read.

accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.issue: Returned HTTP 403 (WebFetch) and HTTP 202 with zero bytes (direct curl, an async bot-challenge response) on multiple attempted entry points.

accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.issue: IEEE Xplore's abstract page is JavaScript-rendered; the fetch tool returned an empty page body.
accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.workaround: Abandoned; the standard's existence and general subject (I, U, P etc. as internationally recognised letter symbols) is well attested by secondary discussion, but per this batch's own rule that search summaries are not evidence, no claim was bound to this source.

accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.candidate: NIST Handbook 44 (2023), full PDF (~5.4MB, hundreds of pages)
accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.issue: The fetch tool could not extract readable text from the compressed PDF stream, and the document is too large to page through blindly to locate the specific Electricity Meters section (3.30) without a known page number.
accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.workaround: Abandoned in favour of the much shorter, directly page-read NISTIR 8248 (NIST Testbed for Examining the Accuracy of Smart Meters), whose introduction explicitly states energy meters measure electrical energy usage.

accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.issue: WebFetch's automatic HTML-conversion step could not render these PDFs' compressed content streams as plain text.
accessFailuresAndWorkarounds.workaround: Each PDF was instead downloaded (the WebFetch tool itself saves the raw bytes to a local file on this failure) and read directly, page by page, with the harness's image-based PDF page reader -- the same workaround used in Batch 03 for SRC-UW-SIMPLEMACHINES and SRC-CUNY-GEARS. Exact passages were read visually from the rendered pages, not inferred from metadata or file names.
